sections.name: Chapter 13 · Healthy Living, Nutrition and Stress

items.q: Which activity increases the production of endorphins, the hormones that produce feelings of well-being?
items.ex: Physical activity stimulates the release of endorphins, which reduce pain and create a sense of well-being (the "runner's high").
w: Good relationships support well-being, but exercise is what's known to trigger endorphin release.
Enjoyable food can lift mood briefly, but the endorphin link taught here is exercise.
Sleep restores the body and mind; it isn't the activity linked to an endorphin boost.

alt.q: Endorphins, the body's "feel-good" hormones, are released most reliably during which activity?
alt.ex: Physical activity stimulates the release of endorphins, which reduce pain and create a sense of well-being (the "runner's high").
w: Being sedentary doesn't trigger endorphin release.
A big meal can cause drowsiness, not an endorphin boost.
Rest is restorative but isn't the endorphin trigger.

tf: Physical activity increases the body's production of endorphins.
Sleeping well is the main way to increase the body's production of endorphins.
Exercise, not sleep, is the activity linked to endorphin release.
ty: Endorphins are released when you engage in physical ________. (one word)
activity
exercise
Physical activity stimulates the release of endorphins, which reduce pain and create a sense of well-being (the "runner's high").

items.q: What is the major reason that smoking is a difficult habit to break?
items.ex: Nicotine is highly addictive. Stopping causes withdrawal symptoms, which makes quitting hard.
w: Most people lack the necessary willpower.
Willpower matters, but the main barrier is physical addiction to nicotine.
It is a good stress reducer.
Smoking feels calming only because it relieves nicotine withdrawal; it isn't a true stress reducer.
Enjoyment isn't the main reason; nicotine dependence is.

alt.q: Why do many smokers find it so hard to quit?
alt.ex: Nicotine is highly addictive. Stopping causes withdrawal symptoms, which makes quitting hard.
w: They don't know smoking is harmful.
Most smokers know the risks; addiction is the barrier.
Cost doesn't explain the difficulty; cigarettes are costly.
Any short-term focus is relief from withdrawal, not a real benefit.

tf: Smoking is hard to quit mainly because nicotine is addictive.
Smoking is hard to quit mainly because it is a good stress reducer.
Nicotine addiction, not stress relief, makes smoking hard to quit.
ty: Smoking is hard to quit because ________ is an addictive substance.
nicotine
Nicotine is highly addictive. Stopping causes withdrawal symptoms, which makes quitting hard.
items.hint: Which chemical in tobacco causes dependence?

items.q: Which statement is true about processed foods?
items.a: Many processed food packages contain more than one serving.
items.ex: Read labels carefully: one package often holds several servings, so the calories, sugar and sodium listed are per serving, not per package.
w: Processed foods contain low amounts of added sugar.
Processed foods are often high in added sugar.
Processed foods tend to have low levels of sodium.
Processed foods are a major source of sodium in the American diet.
Trans fats are not present in processed foods.
Trans fats have been found in processed foods (partially hydrogenated oils).

alt.q: When reading the nutrition label on a packaged snack, what should you check first?
alt.a: How many servings the package contains
alt.ex: Read labels carefully: one package often holds several servings, so the calories, sugar and sodium listed are per serving, not per package.
w: Packaging color tells you nothing about nutrition.
"Natural" is loosely defined; servings per package affect every number on the label.
The brand doesn't change how to read the label.

tf: A single package of processed food often contains more than one serving.
Processed foods tend to be low in sodium.
Processed foods are usually high in sodium, and packages often contain more than one serving.
items.hint: Look at the "servings per container" line on a label.

items.q: Which practice is 100% effective at preventing sexually transmitted diseases?
items.ex: Only abstinence is 100% effective. Condoms, screening and open communication reduce risk but don't eliminate it.
w: Discuss the risk factors with your potential partner.
Talking lowers risk but doesn't guarantee protection.
Get regular screenings because some diseases have no signs or symptoms.
Screening finds infections early; it doesn't prevent them.
Condoms greatly reduce risk but aren't 100% effective.
tf: Abstinence is the only 100% effective way to prevent sexually transmitted diseases.
Using condoms is 100% effective at preventing sexually transmitted diseases.
Condoms reduce risk a lot, but only abstinence is 100% effective.
ty: The only 100% effective way to prevent STDs is ________. (one word)
abstinence
abstaining
abstain
Only abstinence is 100% effective. Condoms, screening and open communication reduce risk but don't eliminate it.
items.hint: It means not having sexual contact at all.

items.q: A deficiency of which mineral can interfere with the blood's ability to carry oxygen?
items.ex: Iron is part of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in red blood cells. Too little iron causes iron-deficiency anemia.
w: Potassium is key for nerve and muscle function, including heart rhythm.
Magnesium supports muscles, nerves and bones, not oxygen transport.
Zinc supports immunity and wound healing.

alt.q: Iron-deficiency anemia reduces the blood's ability to do what?
alt.ex: Iron is part of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in red blood cells. Too little iron causes iron-deficiency anemia.
w: Clotting depends on platelets and clotting factors, not iron.
That's the job of white blood cells.
Iron deficiency doesn't mainly affect temperature control.

tf: Iron deficiency can reduce the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
Zinc deficiency is what reduces the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
Iron, part of hemoglobin, is needed to carry oxygen.
ty: Which mineral is part of hemoglobin and needed to carry oxygen?
iron
Iron is part of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in red blood cells. Too little iron causes iron-deficiency anemia.

items.q: Which term refers to the process of obtaining the food necessary for health and growth?
items.ex: Nutrition is the process of taking in and using the food needed for health and growth.
w: Diet is the food a person usually eats.
Lifestyle is a person's overall way of living.
A habit is any repeated behavior.
tf: Nutrition is the process of obtaining the food necessary for health and growth.
Diet is the process of obtaining the food necessary for health and growth.
That's nutrition; diet is simply what a person usually eats.
ty: The process of obtaining the food needed for health and growth is called ________.
nutrition
Nutrition is the process of taking in and using the food needed for health and growth.

items.q: What happens when someone develops a physical tolerance to a drug?
items.a: They need increasingly higher doses of the drug.
items.ex: Tolerance means the body adapts so the same dose has less effect, and higher doses are needed to get the same result.
w: They can more easily stop using the drug.
Tolerance usually comes with dependence, making it harder to stop.
They receive increased benefits from the drug.
With tolerance, the same dose has less effect.
They need smaller doses of the drug.
tf: A person with drug tolerance needs higher doses to get the same effect.
A person with drug tolerance needs smaller doses to get the same effect.
Tolerance means the same dose works less, so higher doses are needed.
ty: With physical tolerance, a person needs ________ doses to get the same effect. (one word)
higher
larger
bigger
increasing
more
Tolerance means the body adapts so the same dose has less effect, and higher doses are needed to get the same result.
items.hint: The same dose works less and less.

items.q: Which vitamin is necessary for the body to properly absorb calcium?
items.ex: Vitamin D helps the intestines absorb calcium, which keeps bones strong.
w: Vitamin C helps make collagen and heal wounds.
B12 is needed for red blood cells and nerves.
Vitamin A supports vision, skin and immunity.

alt.q: Which vitamin does the skin make in sunlight and helps the body absorb calcium?
alt.ex: Vitamin D helps the intestines absorb calcium, which keeps bones strong.
w: Vitamin K is needed for blood clotting.
Vitamin C supports collagen and wound healing.

tf: Vitamin D is needed for the body to absorb calcium.
Vitamin C is needed for the body to absorb calcium.
Vitamin D (not C) helps absorb calcium; vitamin C helps heal wounds.
ty: Which vitamin helps the body absorb calcium? (letter)
Vitamin D
D
vit D
Vitamin D helps the intestines absorb calcium, which keeps bones strong.

mt.q: Match each vitamin to its main job.
mt.ex: Vitamin D helps the intestines absorb calcium, which keeps bones strong.

items.q: What is believed to be the most serious effect of continual stress?
items.ex: Continual (chronic) stress weakens the immune system, leaving the body more open to illness. This is considered its most serious effect.
w: Stress can affect thinking, but the most serious effect is on immunity and overall health.
That's a real effect, but not the most serious one.
A lowered ability to perform in an emergency
Short-term stress actually helps you react in an emergency.
tf: Continual stress can weaken the immune system.
The most serious effect of continual stress is lowered work efficiency.
The most serious effect is a weakened immune system.
items.hint: Think about how stress affects your ability to fight off illness.

items.q: Which body mass index (BMI) is considered obese?
items.ex: BMI categories: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5–24.9 normal, 25–29.9 overweight, 30 or higher obese.
w: A BMI of 10 is far below normal (severely underweight).

alt.q: A patient's BMI is 31. Which category does this fall in?
alt.ex: BMI categories: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5–24.9 normal, 25–29.9 overweight, 30 or higher obese.

tf: A BMI of 30 or higher is considered obese.
A BMI of 20 is considered obese.
Obese starts at 30; 20 is in the normal range (18.5–24.9).
ty: Obesity starts at a BMI of ____.
BMI categories: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5–24.9 normal, 25–29.9 overweight, 30 or higher obese.

mt.q: Match each BMI to its category.
mt.ex: BMI categories: under 18.5 underweight, 18.5–24.9 normal, 25–29.9 overweight, 30 or higher obese.

items.q: Which nutrients are made of sugar units and provide the body with immediate energy?
items.ex: Carbohydrates are broken down into simple sugars (glucose), the body's quickest energy source.
w: Proteins are made of amino acids and build body structures.
Minerals are elements like iron and calcium; they don't supply energy.
Fats are made of fatty acids and give stored, longer-term energy.
tf: Carbohydrates are made of sugar units and provide immediate energy.
Proteins are made of sugar units and provide immediate energy.
Proteins are made of amino acids; carbohydrates are the sugars that give quick energy.
ty: Nutrients made of sugar units that give immediate energy are ________.
carbohydrates
carbs
carbohydrate
Carbohydrates are broken down into simple sugars (glucose), the body's quickest energy source.

mt.q: Match each nutrient to what it does.
pairs: Amino acids that build body structures
Stored energy; some come from nuts, seeds and olive oil
mt.ex: Carbohydrates are broken down into simple sugars (glucose), the body's quickest energy source.

items.q: Which number is subtracted from a healthy person's age to estimate maximum heart rate when setting an exercise target heart rate?
items.ex: Maximum heart rate ≈ 220 − age. The target range during moderate exercise is about 50–70% of that (higher for vigorous exercise).

alt.q: Using the standard formula, what is the estimated maximum heart rate of a 40-year-old?
alt.ex: Maximum heart rate ≈ 220 − age. The target range during moderate exercise is about 50–70% of that (higher for vigorous exercise).

tf: Maximum heart rate is estimated as 220 minus age.
Maximum heart rate is estimated as 250 minus age.
The formula is 220 − age.
ty: Estimated maximum heart rate = ____ minus age.
Maximum heart rate ≈ 220 − age. The target range during moderate exercise is about 50–70% of that (higher for vigorous exercise).

items.q: Which are physical symptoms of burnout?
items.ex: Burnout shows up physically (fatigue, stomach problems, headaches), emotionally (negative feelings about work) and in behavior (mistakes, absences).
w: That's an emotional sign, not a physical one.
Making errors and taking longer to complete tasks
tf: Fatigue, gastrointestinal disorders and headaches are physical symptoms of burnout.
Increased absences from work are a physical symptom of burnout.
Absences are a behavioral sign; the physical symptoms are fatigue, GI problems and headaches.
items.hint: Look for the choice describing the body, not feelings or behavior.

items.q: Which of these can cause difficulty sleeping if consumed late in the day?
items.ex: Chocolate, tea and cola all contain caffeine, a stimulant that can interfere with sleep.
w: Chocolate has caffeine, but so do the other choices.
Tea has caffeine, but so do the other choices.
Cola has caffeine, but so do the other choices.
tf: Chocolate, tea and cola all contain caffeine that can disturb sleep.
Only cola drinks contain enough caffeine to disturb sleep.
All three contain caffeine and can affect sleep.
ty: Chocolate, tea and cola can disturb sleep because they contain ________.
caffeine
Chocolate, tea and cola all contain caffeine, a stimulant that can interfere with sleep.
items.hint: What do all three have in common?

items.q: Which are common food sources of protein?
items.a: Meats, fish, eggs, legumes and seeds
items.ex: Protein comes from animal foods (meat, fish, eggs, dairy) and plant foods like legumes (beans, lentils), nuts and seeds.
w: These mainly supply vitamins, minerals, fiber and carbohydrates.
tf: Meats, fish, eggs, legumes and seeds are good sources of protein.
Breads, cereals and pastas are the main sources of protein.
Breads and pastas are mainly carbohydrates.
ty: Beans and lentils are called ________, a plant source of protein.
legumes
legume
pulses
Protein comes from animal foods (meat, fish, eggs, dairy) and plant foods like legumes (beans, lentils), nuts and seeds.
items.hint: Think of foods that build muscle.

items.q: Which characteristic is best when setting a health improvement goal?
items.ex: Reasonable, realistic goals are achievable, which keeps motivation up and makes the change last.
w: Too challenging a goal often leads to giving up.
Overly ambitious goals are hard to keep.
The goal should be easy to accomplish.
Too easy a goal doesn't lead to real change.
tf: A health improvement goal should be reasonable.
A health improvement goal should be as ambitious as possible.
Realistic goals are easier to achieve and keep.
ty: A good health goal should be ________ (realistic). (one word)
reasonable
realistic
achievable
attainable
Reasonable, realistic goals are achievable, which keeps motivation up and makes the change last.
items.hint: Not too hard, not too easy.

items.q: What information does MyPlate, from the U.S. Department of Agriculture, provide?
items.a: Recommended proportions of healthy food groups
items.ex: MyPlate shows how to balance a meal: about half fruits and vegetables, plus grains, protein and dairy.
w: How many calories to consume each day
MyPlate shows proportions of food groups, not a daily calorie number.
The type of diet to follow
It's a general guide to balance, not a specific diet plan.
tf: MyPlate shows the recommended proportions of the healthy food groups.
MyPlate tells you exactly how many calories to eat each day.
MyPlate is about proportions of food groups, not calorie counts.
ty: MyPlate was developed by the U.S. Department of ________.
Agriculture
USDA
MyPlate shows how to balance a meal: about half fruits and vegetables, plus grains, protein and dairy.
items.hint: It's a picture of a plate divided into sections.

items.q: Which employees must be offered the hepatitis B vaccination by their employer?
items.a: Workers who are exposed to patients' bodily fluids
items.ex: OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard requires employers to offer the hepatitis B vaccine, free of charge, to workers with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials.
w: All workers in clinics and hospitals
It's required based on exposure, not just workplace.
Workers who care for elderly patients
Age of patients isn't the criterion; exposure to blood or body fluids is.
Workers at high risk for illness
The rule is about occupational exposure to blood and body fluids.
tf: Employers must offer the hepatitis B vaccine to workers exposed to blood or body fluids.
Employers must offer the hepatitis B vaccine only to workers who care for elderly patients.
It's based on exposure to blood or body fluids (OSHA).
ty: Employers must offer workers exposed to body fluids the hepatitis ___ vaccine. (letter)
B
OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard requires employers to offer the hepatitis B vaccine, free of charge, to workers with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials.
items.hint: It's about exposure to blood and body fluids (OSHA).

items.q: What is the first step to successfully changing a habit?
items.a: Be willing to change the habit.
items.ex: Change starts with being willing (motivated) to change. Planning, tracking, support and rewards come next.
w: Decide how you will track your progress.
Tracking helps, but it comes after deciding to change.
Set up a good support system.
Support helps, but willingness comes first.
Rewards help, but only once you've committed to change.
tf: The first step in changing a habit is being willing to change it.
The first step in changing a habit is planning rewards.
Willingness comes first; rewards and tracking come after.
items.hint: Nothing else works until this is in place.

items.q: Which STD should everyone aged 13–64 be tested for at least once as part of routine health care, and more often with multiple partners?
items.ex: The CDC recommends that everyone aged 13–64 be tested for HIV at least once, and those at higher risk at least yearly.
w: Routine chlamydia screening targets sexually active women under 25 and others at risk.
Syphilis screening is risk-based and in pregnancy.
Routine herpes testing isn't recommended for people without symptoms.
tf: The CDC recommends everyone aged 13–64 be tested for HIV at least once.
The CDC recommends everyone aged 13–64 be tested for genital herpes at least once.
The universal once-in-a-lifetime test is for HIV.
ty: Everyone aged 13–64 should be tested at least once for ____. (abbreviation)
HIV
human immunodeficiency virus
The CDC recommends that everyone aged 13–64 be tested for HIV at least once, and those at higher risk at least yearly.
items.hint: It's the virus that causes AIDS.

items.q: Which is an example of an internal stressor?
items.ex: Internal stressors come from within the person, such as habits, attitudes and skills like poor time management. External stressors come from the environment or other people.
w: That comes from the environment: an external stressor.
That's another person: an external stressor.
That's imposed from outside: an external stressor.
tf: Poor time management skills are an internal stressor.
A demanding supervisor is an internal stressor.
A supervisor is external; internal stressors come from within, like poor time management.
items.hint: Internal = something about the person themselves.

items.q: Which is a characteristic of bulimia?
items.a: Eating large amounts of food followed by self-induced vomiting
items.ex: Bulimia nervosa involves binge eating followed by purging, such as self-induced vomiting or laxative use.
w: Uncontrolled eating beyond the satisfaction of hunger
That describes binge eating without purging.
Eating far fewer calories than the body needs
tf: Bulimia involves binge eating followed by purging, such as self-induced vomiting.
Bulimia involves eating far fewer calories than the body needs.
That's anorexia; bulimia is binge eating then purging.
ty: Bulimia is binge eating followed by ________ (vomiting or laxatives).
purging
purge
vomiting
Bulimia nervosa involves binge eating followed by purging, such as self-induced vomiting or laxative use.

items.q: Which communication technique lets you express feelings freely in a nonthreatening manner?
items.ex: Assertiveness means stating your feelings and needs honestly and respectfully, without being passive or aggressive.
w: That's organizing your time, not a communication style.
Mediation is a third party helping others settle a dispute.
tf: Assertiveness is expressing feelings freely in a nonthreatening manner.
Mediation is expressing your own feelings freely in a nonthreatening manner.
Mediation involves a third party; assertiveness is your own respectful expression.
ty: Expressing your feelings honestly but respectfully is called ________.
assertiveness
assertive
being assertive
Assertiveness means stating your feelings and needs honestly and respectfully, without being passive or aggressive.

items.q: Which statement accurately describes the relationship between personal health habits and major causes of death?
items.a: Unhealthy lifestyle habits increase the risk of chronic diseases and premature death.
items.ex: Many leading causes of death, like heart disease, some cancers and diabetes, are strongly influenced by habits such as smoking, diet, activity and stress.
w: Major causes of death are primarily determined by genetic factors.
Genes play a role, but lifestyle strongly influences heart disease, cancer and diabetes.
Leading a sedentary lifestyle has no consequences for health.
Inactivity raises the risk of heart disease, diabetes and obesity.
Personal health habits have no impact on major causes of death.
Habits like smoking, diet and exercise strongly affect leading causes of death.

sc.title: Reggie, nurse practitioner
sc.text: Reggie is a nurse practitioner in a primary care clinic who is passionate about promoting health and wellness. Reggie leads by example: regular exercise, healthy eating, good sleep and low stress. Reggie starts the day with a breakfast of fruits, whole grains and protein, drinks water through the day, and uses breaks to stretch and walk around the neighborhood. Reggie encourages patients to adopt similar, realistic healthy habits and gives them resources and support.

items.hint: Reggie's habits are meant to lower which risks?

items.q: Why is it significant for health care professionals like Reggie to maintain a healthy lifestyle?
items.a: To set a good example for patients and promote health and wellness
items.ex: Health care workers who model healthy habits are more credible when teaching patients, and they stay healthier themselves.
w: Appearance isn't the point of healthy habits.
To increase productivity and efficiency at work
That can be a side benefit, but the main reason is modeling health for patients.
To avoid disciplinary action from regulatory bodies
Personal habits like diet aren't regulated this way.

items.q: What is one strategy Reggie can use to reduce the risk of burnout?
items.a: Cultivating a healthy work-life balance and seeking social support
items.ex: Burnout is prevented by balance, rest, leisure, social support and paying attention to stress.
w: Ignoring signs of stress and overworking
Bottling up emotions so they don't affect patient care
Suppressing emotions increases stress; support helps.
tf: Work-life balance and social support help prevent burnout.
Avoiding breaks helps prevent burnout.
Breaks, balance and support prevent burnout.

items.q: What are the key principles of good nutrition?
items.a: Balancing macronutrients like carbohydrates, proteins and fats
items.ex: Good nutrition means a balanced intake of carbohydrates, proteins and healthy fats, plus vitamins, minerals, fiber and water.
w: Processed foods are often high in sugar, sodium and unhealthy fats.
Eliminating all fats from the diet
Carbohydrates are the body's main energy source.

Good nutrition requires eliminating all fats.
The body needs healthy fats; balance is the key.

items.q: Which eating disorder is most likely to be life-threatening?
items.ex: Anorexia nervosa has the highest death rate of any mental illness, from starvation, heart problems and suicide.
w: Binge eating disorder carries health risks but is less often fatal.
Bulimia is dangerous, but anorexia has the highest death rate.
Purging is a behavior, not a separate eating disorder.
tf: Anorexia nervosa is the eating disorder most likely to be life-threatening.
Binge eating is the eating disorder most likely to be life-threatening.
Anorexia has the highest death rate.
ty: The eating disorder with the highest death rate is anorexia ________.
nervosa
Anorexia nervosa has the highest death rate of any mental illness, from starvation, heart problems and suicide.

items.q: Tracking your progress in writing can be helpful when working to adopt new habits.
items.ex: Writing down progress keeps you accountable and shows you how far you've come.
items.ww: Tracking is a proven aid to changing habits.

alt.q: Keeping a written record of your progress makes it harder to adopt new habits.
alt.ex: Tracking in writing helps you stay accountable.

items.q: Which food group is emphasized most on the MyPlate icon?
items.ex: On MyPlate, vegetables take up the largest section; fruits and vegetables together make up half the plate.
w: Protein is a smaller section of the plate.
Fruits share the half, but vegetables are the largest section.
Dairy is shown as a cup beside the plate.

Protein takes up the largest section of MyPlate.
Vegetables are the largest section.
ty: The largest section of MyPlate is ________.
vegetables
veggies
vegetable

items.q: To benefit from meditation, what is the minimum time a person should plan to spend in each session?
items.ex: A common guideline (and the one taught in this course) is to meditate at least 20 minutes per session, once or twice a day.
w: Short sessions help, but the guideline taught is at least 20 minutes.
The guideline taught is at least 20 minutes.
The guideline taught is at least 20 minutes.
tf: A meditation session should last at least 20 minutes to get the full benefit.
A meditation session needs only 5 minutes to get the full benefit.
The guideline taught is at least 20 minutes.
ty: Plan at least ____ minutes per meditation session.
twenty
A common guideline (and the one taught in this course) is to meditate at least 20 minutes per session, once or twice a day.

items.q: Fats needed by the body can only be obtained from animal sources, such as meat and fish.
items.ex: Healthy fats also come from plants: olive oil, nuts, seeds and avocados.
items.ww: Plant foods like nuts, seeds, olives and avocados also supply needed fats.

alt.q: Olive oil, nuts and avocados are plant sources of healthy fats.
alt.ex: Plants are good sources of healthy fats.
alt.ww: They are plant sources of healthy, unsaturated fats.

items.q: Which nutrient consists of amino acids that build the body's structural components?
items.ex: Proteins are made of amino acids and build and repair muscles, organs, skin and other tissues.
w: Minerals are elements like calcium and iron.
Fiber is indigestible plant material that aids digestion.
Carbohydrates are sugars used for energy.
tf: Proteins are made of amino acids that build body structures.
Carbohydrates are made of amino acids that build body structures.
Amino acids make up proteins; carbohydrates are sugars.
ty: Proteins are made of ________ ________. (two words)
amino acids
amino acid
Proteins are made of amino acids and build and repair muscles, organs, skin and other tissues.

mt.q: Match each nutrient to what it does.
pairs: Amino acids that build body structures
Stored energy; some come from nuts, seeds and olive oil
mt.ex: Proteins are made of amino acids and build and repair muscles, organs, skin and other tissues.

items.q: How do trans fats potentially harm the body?
items.a: By raising LDL ("bad") cholesterol while lowering HDL ("good") cholesterol
items.ex: Trans fats raise LDL and lower HDL, increasing the risk of heart disease. Partially hydrogenated oils were the main source.
w: That isn't the main harm of trans fats.
Any fat is calorie-dense, but the specific harm is to cholesterol levels.
By blocking the absorption of vitamins
That isn't how trans fats harm the body.
tf: Trans fats raise LDL cholesterol and lower HDL cholesterol.
Trans fats lower LDL cholesterol and raise HDL cholesterol.
Trans fats do the opposite: raise LDL, lower HDL.

items.q: What determines how you view situations and can be either positive or negative?
items.ex: Attitude is your general way of viewing situations, positive or negative, and it shapes how you handle stress.
w: Opinions are views on specific topics.
Emotions are feelings that come and go; attitude is your overall outlook.
Stress is a reaction, not an outlook.
tf: Your attitude determines how you view situations and can be positive or negative.
Stress determines how you view situations and can be positive or negative.
That describes attitude.
ty: Your overall positive or negative outlook is your ________.
attitude
Attitude is your general way of viewing situations, positive or negative, and it shapes how you handle stress.

items.q: Which statement is true about stress?
items.a: It is the body's physical reaction to perceived danger.
items.ex: Stress is the body's "fight-or-flight" reaction to perceived danger. Short-term stress can help; continual stress harms health.
w: Every effort should be made to avoid it.
Some stress is normal and even helpful; the goal is managing it.
Continual stress is not harmful if a person learns to adjust to it.

items.q: Which food is NOT a cholesterol-lowering food?

Walnuts contain healthy fats that help lower cholesterol.

Oatmeal raises cholesterol.

beef

Not knowing where to get help

Withdrawal discomfort is the major barrier.

withdrawal

items.q: About what percentage of American teenagers were reported to have obesity in 2020?

It was about 22%.

Normal stops at 24.9.

A normal BMI is 18.5 to 24.9. 25–29.9 is overweight and 30+ is obese.

items.q: When working to develop new habits, it helps to reward yourself when you reach your goals.

items.q: Heart disease, diabetes and osteoporosis can be prevented by which habit?

Avoiding all stress isn't possible or the answer.

Exercise is the preventive habit.

exercise
activity

items.q: Which is NOT an effective way to lower blood pressure?

Less salt lowers blood pressure.

items.q: The Mediterranean diet recommends at least how many servings of fish or shellfish each week?

It's at least two.

two
The Mediterranean diet emphasizes vegetables, fruits, whole grains, olive oil and at least two servings of fish or seafood a week.

fibre

items.q: Which is the best description of Maslow's hierarchy of human needs?
items.a: Categories of needs ranked in order of importance
items.ex: Maslow ranked human needs in levels; lower, more basic needs generally must be met before higher ones. Maslow's levels, bottom to top: physiological (food, water, shelter) → safety and security → love and belonging (affection) → self-esteem → self-actualization (reaching full potential).
w: The hierarchy is about the needs themselves, not reactions to them.
It covers all human needs, not only health care.
It ranks needs; it doesn't describe behaviors.
tf: Maslow's hierarchy ranks categories of needs in order of importance.
Maslow's hierarchy describes behaviors people use in response to needs.
It's a ranking of needs, not behaviors.

items.q: Which is true of someone who has high self-esteem?
items.ex: Self-esteem means valuing and respecting yourself. It's the fourth level of Maslow's hierarchy.

Self-esteem is self-respect.

respect
worth
value
Self-esteem means valuing and respecting yourself. It's the fourth level of Maslow's hierarchy.

That's about reaching one's full potential.

safety

mt.q: Match each level of Maslow's hierarchy to what it means.

items.q: What can health care professionals do to help patients deal with loss?

Humors are body fluids.

fluids
fluid

Yin and yang come from Chinese tradition.

items.q: Communicating to patients that they are worth your time helps them with which need?
items.ex: Showing patients they matter supports their self-esteem. Maslow's levels, bottom to top: physiological (food, water, shelter) → safety and security → love and belonging (affection) → self-esteem → self-actualization (reaching full potential).

items.q: According to some cultures, which must be integrated and in balance for good health?

The usual trio is mind, body and spirit.

The belief is about mind, body and spirit.

spirit
soul

items.q: Which is an example of prejudice?

prejudice

culture

sc.title: David, family counselor
sc.text: David is a family counselor who works with families from many cultural backgrounds. He meets with the Garcia family, who recently immigrated from Mexico. They are adapting to a new environment, facing communication barriers and conflict at home, and don't yet feel they belong in their new community. David listens attentively, considers their cultural background and values, respects their individual differences, and creates a safe, culturally sensitive environment to help them through the transition and strengthen their relationships.

items.q: Why is it important for David to understand cultural differences in physical contact and personal space?

Respect means accommodating, not correcting them.

items.ex: Body language, facial expressions, tone and gestures can carry up to 70% of a message's meaning.
w: Verbal and nonverbal communication usually express equal amounts of meaning.
Nonverbal communication usually carries more of the meaning.
It only reinforces the meaning of the verbal message.
It can also contradict the words.
It expresses a small part of the message's meaning.
tf: Nonverbal communication can express up to 70% of the sender's meaning.
Nonverbal communication expresses only a small part of a message's meaning.
It can carry up to 70%.
ty: Nonverbal communication can express up to ____% of a message's meaning.
Body language, facial expressions, tone and gestures can carry up to 70% of a message's meaning.

items.q: Why do some people with limited vision also have trouble understanding spoken communication?
items.a: They can't see body language and facial expressions.
items.ex: Much of meaning is nonverbal; people who can't see it miss part of the message, so describe what you're doing and use tone carefully.
w: Vision and hearing are separate senses.
They don't know who is talking to them.
That can happen, but the main loss is nonverbal cues.
items.hint: Think about the nonverbal part of a message.

items.q: Which is true about patients who are terminally ill?
items.a: Many have a strong need to share their fears and concerns.
items.ex: Dying patients often want to talk about their fears. Listening and giving opportunities to express feelings helps.
w: Most prefer to be left alone.
Many want company and someone to listen.
Near the end of life they can no longer speak or hear.
Hearing often remains until the very end.
tf: Many terminally ill patients have a strong need to share their fears.
Most dying patients prefer to be left alone.
Many want to talk and be heard.

items.q: What is a health care worker demonstrating by fully focusing on what a patient is saying?
items.ex: Active listening means giving full attention, concentrating and observing, not just hearing words.
ty: Fully focusing on what someone is saying is called ________ listening.
active
Active listening means giving full attention, concentrating and observing, not just hearing words.

items.q: Which is NOT necessarily a good way to maintain patients' self-esteem?
items.ex: Efficiency matters, but rushing can make patients feel unimportant. Respect, privacy and involvement support self-esteem.
w: Involve patients in decisions about their health.
items.hint: Which one is about you, not the patient?

items.q: What is the first step in the communication process?
items.ex: Steps of the communication process: set communication goals → create the message → deliver the message → listen to the response (and obtain feedback) → evaluate the communication throughout.
tf: The first step in the communication process is setting communication goals.
The first step in the communication process is delivering the message.
Goals come first.
items.hint: Know what you want to achieve.

items.q: Which is a way to obtain feedback?
items.ex: Feedback techniques include reflecting, paraphrasing, asking questions and requesting examples.
w: Yes, but the others are also feedback techniques.
Yes, but the others are also feedback techniques.
Yes, but the others are also feedback techniques.

items.q: When should a health care worker evaluate communication with a patient?
items.ex: Evaluate continuously so you can adjust as you go. Steps of the communication process: set communication goals → create the message → deliver the message → listen to the response (and obtain feedback) → evaluate the communication throughout.
w: Evaluation shouldn't wait for one step.
At the end of the conversation
By then it may be too late to fix misunderstandings.
Feedback helps, but evaluation is continuous.

items.q: About what percentage of Americans aged 75 and older have significant hearing loss?
items.ex: About half of adults aged 75 and older have disabling hearing loss (NIDCD).
w: Too low for this age group.
Too low for this age group.
Close, but about half of adults 75+ have disabling hearing loss.

About 20% of Americans 75 and older have significant hearing loss.
It's about half.

items.q: Two health care workers laugh in the break room about a coworker's "weird clothes." This conversation is:
items.ex: Gossip damages teamwork and trust. It's unprofessional anywhere.
w: Acceptable if the coworker can't hear
Gossip is unprofessional whether or not they hear.
Okay as long as they're on break
Okay if it's not done in the workplace
Gossip about coworkers is harmful anywhere.

items.q: When caring for patients who are terminally ill, health care professionals should:
items.a: Give them opportunities to express their feelings

w: Make an effort not to disturb them

items.q: What is feedback in communication intended to do?
items.a: Help both senders and receivers increase their understanding of each other
items.ex: Feedback lets both sides check understanding: the sender learns if the message was received as intended, and the receiver confirms what they heard.
w: Increase the interaction between senders and receivers
More interaction isn't the goal; understanding is.
Only help listeners know whether they understood
It helps both sides, not only the listener.
Only help senders know whether their message was interpreted correctly
It helps both sides, not only the sender.

items.q: Touching a patient's shoulder or hand can be an effective way of communicating.

items.q: If a patient says they're "fine" but their body language shows they're worried, they are most likely:
items.ex: When verbal and nonverbal messages conflict, the nonverbal message is usually the true one.
w: When words and body language conflict, body language is usually more accurate.
The message is mixed, but the nonverbal part shows the real feeling.
tf: When words and body language conflict, body language usually shows the true feeling.
When words and body language conflict, the words usually show the true feeling.
Body language is usually more accurate.

items.q: When speaking to an older woman who is a new patient, the medical assistant should:
items.a: Ask the patient how she wishes to be addressed
items.ex: Ask patients how they'd like to be addressed. Until then, use a title and last name.
w: Call the patient by her first name
First names may seem disrespectful to some older adults.

items.q: Which is appropriate when communicating with someone who has hearing loss?
items.a: Direct a light source on your face.
items.ex: Good lighting on your face helps the person read lips and expressions. Face them, speak clearly and pause.
w: Face the person so they can see your lips and expressions.

tf: Lighting your face helps a person with hearing loss read your lips.
Sitting next to a person with hearing loss helps them understand you.
Face them instead so they can see your lips.

items.q: The physical environment can influence how effective communication is.
items.ex: Noise, lighting, privacy and comfort all affect communication.

items.q: With which patient might pantomime be an effective way to communicate?
items.a: A patient who understands very little English

w: A patient who is almost completely blind

A patient who is very upset

items.q: A patient with Alzheimer's disease says it's Sunday when it's Tuesday. What is the best response?

Asking them to reason it out can frustrate them.

items.q: To control your nerves when speaking to a group, it's best not to look at the audience.
items.ex: Eye contact helps you connect and stay engaged; practice and preparation help with nerves.

items.q: Which is an example of a good learning objective?

items.q: Which question is most likely to help a nurse learn about a patient's needs?

items.q: Today's patients need more education and information from health care professionals than in the past.

items.ww: Reactions can get in the way of listening.

items.ex: We can think much faster than people speak, which is why the mind can wander while listening.
items.ww: The mind works faster than speech.

items.q: A patient just learned they have cancer and feels depressed. What is the best thing to do?

items.q: Many Americans read only at a grade-school level and don't understand instructions on prescription bottles.

items.q: The health care professional can enhance a patient's self-esteem by communicating courteously and respectfully.

items.q: Which is the best example of successful communication by a pharmacy technician explaining a new medication?
items.a: The technician used feedback and determined that the customer understood the instructions.

paraphrase

items.q: Touch is a nonverbal form of communication that can be used with all patients to show care and interest.

items.q: Which is a recommendation for good telephone communication?
items.a: Smile as you speak, unless it's inappropriate.
items.ex: Smiling changes your tone of voice and makes you sound friendly on the phone.
w: Speak clearly at a moderate, not slow, pace.
items.hint: People can hear it in your voice.

items.q: It is important for health care professionals to control their facial expressions with patients.
items.ex: Expressions of shock or disgust can upset patients; keep a calm, caring expression.

items.q: Speaking a little louder than normal helps non-English speakers understand you.
items.ex: Volume doesn't help with a language barrier. Use simple words, gestures and an interpreter.
items.ww: Louder doesn't fix a language barrier.

items.q: Which is NOT a helpful technique for communicating with someone who has dementia?
items.ex: With dementia: use simple words, repeat the same words rather than rephrasing, and don't argue or reason. Long, unfilled pauses can lose the person's attention, so this is the choice the course marks as not helpful (giving a little time to respond is still good).
w: Don't try to reason with the patient.
Reasoning and arguing frustrate people with dementia, so this is helpful advice.
Repeat rather than rephrase if the patient doesn't understand.
Repeating the same words is less confusing, so this is helpful.

items.q: What type of question is "What is your date of birth?"

close
Closed-ended questions have a short, specific answer, like a date or yes/no.

mt.q: Match each type of question to an example.
pairs: "Can you tell me more about that?"
mt.ex: Closed-ended questions have a short, specific answer, like a date or yes/no.

items.q: Humor is usually not appropriate for patients who are ill or injured.
items.ex: Gentle, appropriate humor can relieve tension; read the situation and the patient.

items.q: Many patients don't understand the information they're given but are too embarrassed to admit it.

items.q: Communication among health care professionals is as important as communication with patients.

items.ww: Team communication is critical to safety.

mt.q: Match each type of question to an example.
pairs: "Can you tell me more about that?"
mt.ex: Probing questions follow up to get more detail about something the patient has already mentioned.

items.q: Which website extension is used by agencies such as the National Institutes of Health and the Food and Drug Administration?

Government agencies like the NIH and FDA use .com web addresses.
.com is commercial; government sites use .gov.

.gov
gov

items.q: Which law specifically addresses the privacy of medical records?

A.D.A.M. is a medical information resource, not a law.

FAERS is the law that protects the privacy of medical records.
FAERS is a drug-safety database; HIPAA is the privacy law.

HIPAA
HIPAA sets national rules protecting the privacy and security of patients' health information.

items.q: What does it mean to be a computer-literate health care professional?
items.a: Having the knowledge and skills to perform the computer tasks your job requires
items.ex: Computer literacy means being able to efficiently do the computer tasks required for your own job.

Research is one possible task, not the definition.
tf: Computer literacy means having the skills to perform the computer tasks your job requires.

items.q: Which is NOT a guideline for writing professional emails?

optics

Permission to install software on more than one computer

About 75% (the CDC now cites about 90% including mental health).

items.q: Which payment method is catastrophic when costs exceed the patient's ability to pay?

sc.title: Josie, pharmacy technician
sc.text: Josie is a pharmacy technician in a busy hospital pharmacy who prepares and dispenses medications and helps make medication use accurate and safe.
